source.title: Twin: Tuning Learning Rate and Weight Decay of Deep Homogeneous Classifiers without Validation

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests validation-free predictors of generalization with train-test loss scaling and post-hoc sharpness selection, but does not test the specific interventions and settings in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Reports results for worst-case m-sharpness selection and a fitted train-test loss scaling law. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows. Values used to choose the 15% training-accuracy filter and the separability threshold are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: Table 4 contains results bearing on V3: convolutional classifiers outperform fully connected classifiers trained from scratch on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The sharpness-selection and scaling-law rows do not test the specified versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose a regime-dependent predictor using training loss in non-separable pools and parameter norms among approximately separable models. Twin achieves 1.28 percentage points mean absolute accuracy error against test-set Oracle selection across 37 configurations. They qualify the scaling law as empirical and acknowledge noisy transfer-learning regimes. Their m-sharpness comparison concerns selection reliability, not a direct test of V7.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops validation-free hyperparameter selection and evaluates train-test loss scaling and worst-case m-sharpness selection; it does not reproduce the listed studies' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports changes in selection performance across dataset and model class, and sensitivity to separability threshold and scheduler. Transfer-learning domain overlap makes the train-test relation noisier and changes the MAE; stronger early stopping reduces the MAE in some overlapping domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Filtered m-sharpness selection averages 71.3% test accuracy versus Twin's 73.4%; differences are larger on transformers and small on convolutional networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Absolute-radius worst-case m-sharpness can be less effective than Twin for selecting LR–WD configurations in these image-classification searches.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted train–test loss relation has global R² 0.896 and per-configuration log-space R² mean 0.792 and median 0.955.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A phenomenological train–test loss scaling relation fits many of the evaluated image-classification hyperparameter pools.

record.problems: The scaling law is explicitly phenomenological rather than universally established; the derivation assumes a noiseless relation and simplifies smoothed margin and homogeneity. The study is restricted to image classification. Table 1 reports selection accuracies but no uncertainty estimates. The stated m-sharpness result is about selection performance, not a direct correlation coefficient or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for cited findings from other studies. The many per-configuration scaling-law plots in Figures 3, 9, and 10 are not individually enumerated; the text reports aggregate fit statistics and qualitative descriptions instead. Optimizer comparison Table 6 reports Twin's selection performance and (M)AE, not optimizer generalization effects as named by the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for interpolation.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, convolution-derived initialization, and comparisons on MNIST and SVHN.
Comparable adaptive-versus-SGD experiments establishing generalization differences under the specified tuning conditions; Table 6 evaluates Twin under alternative optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, weight decay, or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: Record the CIFAR-10 architecture comparison: MLP-4-256 versus RNX11, base augmentation, Oracle/SelVS/Twin accuracies respectively 66.1/65.9/65.1% versus 90.7/90.6/90.2%. These results consistently favor the convolutional classifier.

Record the CIFAR-100 architecture comparison: MLP-4-512 versus WRN-40-2, medium augmentation, Oracle/SelVS/Twin accuracies respectively 35.4/35.1/34.9% versus 74.2/72.8/74.2%. Note differing architecture sizes and tuning-trial counts.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks incidental evidence for V3 in Table 4. These architecture comparisons support the performance difference in the tested settings but do not isolate local connectivity as its cause. All existing rows remain outside the listed versions; no verdict follows from their extracted states.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy under natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader optimizer tuning.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and its interaction with weight decay or data augmentation.

Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their ranking of train-test gaps among similarly trained networks. The study evaluates worst-case m-sharpness as a selection proxy, not the magnitude-aware measure specified in this version.
Removing and retraining after removing memorized training examples.
